questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: identify which operation keeps the solution set unchanged
questions.stem: A student wants to simplify 4x plus 7 equals 19 without changing which values of x work. She considers four moves. Which move is guaranteed to preserve the solution set?

options.text: Subtract 7 from both sides, because the same change on both sides balances the equation
Subtract 7 from the left side only, because the constant is only on that side
options.misconception: believes an operation on one side can be applied to a single term

options.text: Divide the left side by 4 only, because the coefficient is attached to x
options.misconception: thinks division can target one side while leaving the other unchanged

options.text: Multiply the left side by 2 only, because doubling simplifies the coefficient
options.misconception: assumes scaling one side keeps the equation balanced

questions.explanation: Adding or subtracting the same quantity on both sides, or multiplying or dividing both sides by the same nonzero quantity, produces an equivalent equation with the same solutions. Subtracting 7 only from the left would change the balance and introduce a different solution set. The trap is treating the operation as something that can be applied to a single side or term.
questions.hint: Ask whether the same change is applied to both sides.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: explain why division by a variable expression requires a nonzero condition
questions.stem: A student solves 3x equals 2x by dividing both sides by x and concluding x equals 1. What is the flaw in that reasoning?

options.text: Division by x is always valid, so the original equation really has only one solution
options.misconception: assumes a variable divisor is never zero

options.text: Division by x is only valid when x is not zero, and x equals 0 also satisfies the original equation
The student should have subtracted 2x first, because division is never allowed in equations
options.misconception: believes division is forbidden when solving linear equations

options.text: The flaw is that 3x and 2x cannot be compared, because they have different coefficients
options.misconception: thinks different coefficients make an equation unsolvable

questions.explanation: Dividing both sides by x assumes x is not zero, since division by zero is undefined. The original equation 3x equals 2x simplifies to x equals 0, so zero is a solution that the division step silently discards. The trap is treating the variable as though it were a known nonzero number.

options.text: Adding 5 to both sides, because constants change the balance

options.text: Squaring both sides, because it can introduce extraneous solutions
Subtracting x from both sides, because the variable disappears

questions.explanation: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing both sides by the same nonzero quantity preserves solutions.
